reaudit_note: Mechanical re-stamp by `./le rfc reseal`. Every verdict re-stamped below was in the SHIFTED state: its recorded unit fingerprints -- the enclosing top-level function of each tagged test -- were byte-identical to the tree, and only the file around them had moved (a line shift, a sibling test, an import rewrite). Nothing about what any of these tests asserts changed, so no verdict was re-judged and only the `tests` map was rewritten. A verdict whose unit, cited producer code, or requirement text moved was REFUSED and left stale for a human. The proof is the code in verdict_freshness(), not this note.

RFC905-x-1.note: Unchanged on re-read after TestISISChecksumDetectsCorruption lost its x-3 tag. B.2 fixes addition modulo 255, or one's complement with 255 read as 0. Only TestISISChecksumFixedVector (0x0b,0xed) goes red on a mod-256 generator; TestISISChecksumModulus round-trips Checksum through VerifyChecksum, which share fletcherModulus, so a consistent mod-256 change still verifies. The negative TestISISChecksumDetectsCorruption flips single octets, which a mod-256 verifier also detects. Clause b (255 read as 0) has no assertion that catches a verifier treating 255 and 0 as distinct.

RFC905-x-2.note: Unchanged on re-read after TestISISChecksumDetectsCorruption lost its x-3 tag. The quote is B.3.3: C0 += octet, then C1 += C0. The positive TestISISChecksumVectors goes red on a wrong generator accumulation through the round trip. The negative TestISISChecksumDetectsCorruption asserts only that VerifyChecksum rejects corrupted regions, the RFC905-x-4 assertion wearing a second hat; it feeds no input that violates B.3.3 (for example the C1 += octet order or a skipped octet), so no negative isolates this rule.

RFC905-x-3.note: B.3.4 X = -C1 + (L-n).C0, Y = C1 - (L-n+1).C0. Positive: TestISISChecksumMatchesClosedForm (Checksum) and TestFletcherGenerateMatchesClosedForm (fletcherGenerate) compare the producer at every field offset 0..L-2 of a 24-octet region against an independent B.3.3/B.3.4 re-derivation written in the RFC's own L-n notation, so any formula change at any n goes red without a verifier in the loop; TestISISChecksumFixedVector and TestFletcherRFC905Vectors pin fixed values. Negative: TestISISChecksumRefusesMisplacedXY and TestFletcherGenerateRefusesMisplacedXY put a pair that is not the formula's value at n,n+1 (Y,X swapped, or X,Y one octet early, guarded against X == Y) and the verifier refuses it, while the formula's pair at n,n+1 is accepted. B.1 defines X and Y as the octets at n and n+1, so a wrong value there violates this formula; the B.3.5 placement obligation remains split out of the row.

RFC905-x-4.note: B.4.3: the check fails when either or both of C0 and C1 is non-zero. TestISISVerifyRequiresBothSumsZero (VerifyChecksum) and TestFletcherVerifyRequiresBothSumsZero (fletcherVerify) now feed a region with C0 zero and C1 non-zero (octets 2 and 3 swapped, asserted unequal) and one with C1 zero and C0 non-zero (+1 then -2 on the last two octets), and both are refused; the unmodified generated region is accepted. A verifier reading only C0, or only C1, or requiring both non-zero goes red (mutant records && -> ||). The both-non-zero case stays covered by the single-octet flips of TestISISChecksumDetectsCorruption and TestOSPFLSAChecksumExcludesAge.
